tests.scope: Offline exact arithmetic, native recording and supplied/mock provenance; no live CAS requested.

soundness_argument: Assuming ordered endpoints and exact rational polynomial interpretation, Sturm variations certify one selected real root. A common gcd with a root in that interval proves zero there. Otherwise interval Horner bounds after root-preserving bisection establish strict sign, or exact evaluation handles a rational root. Endpoint roots require removal of full multiplicity and exclusion of other roots. Complete receipt recomputation plus relation/sign comparison binds the conclusion to the declared expression and selected embedding.
findings: Producer/checker dense arithmetic is separately authored but shares the groebner parser, rational arithmetic platform and Sturm theorem premise; this is not fully independent TCBs.
Repeated interior roots, gcd-zero and repeated endpoint roots agree in direct controls.
Both direct APIs accept a reversed interval when an endpoint is a root. Native model validation refuses lo>=hi, so no native-log admission bypass demonstrated.
Producer validates max_refinements in 0..256; expected_receipt lacks that direct parameter guard, while verify always uses the default.
Degree/coefficient limits and refinement cap do not establish a whole-request arithmetic bit-growth bound.
Receipts retain embedding by reference; mutation tests use deepcopy. Full recomputation remains necessary, not stored object immutability.
proposed_repairs: Validate ordered interval endpoints and refinement bounds at both standalone API boundaries, retaining native validation too.
Describe checker independence precisely and preserve shared-parser assumptions in the TCB inventory.
remaining: Portable extraction of uncovered repeated-root/direct API controls and broader malformed/budget behavior remain.
No Lean soundness implementation or new checker admission performed.
